sentences.text: Hello everyone. Welcome to the Slow English Podcast. I'm Emili, and today we are traveling to Africa,
to the beautiful city of Dakar in Senegal. Dakar is full of music, colors, and life.
It is a city by the Atlantic Ocean with beautiful beaches and kind people. Let's explore this
amazing African city together. Part two, where is Dakar? Dakar is the capital city of Senegal.
It is in West Africa on the very edge of the continent. The city is surrounded by the ocean.
From Dakar, you can see the waves and the sunset every evening. It is one of the most important
cities in West Africa for culture, music, and trade. Part three, a short history of Dakar.
Dakar has a long and deep history. Many years ago, it was a small fishing village. Later,
it became an important port for ships from Europe. Sadly, during history, Dakar was also a place
connected to the slave trade. You can visit Gore Island, a small island near Dakar, to learn
about this painful past. Today, the island is a symbol of peace, memory, and hope. Part four,
the city and its streets. Dakar is big, busy, and full of energy. There are cars, buses, and many
people walking and talking everywhere. You can see colorful markets, small shops, and street food
stands. The buildings are a mix of modern and traditional styles. There are also quiet places,
parks and beaches where you can rest and watch the ocean. Part five, the people of Dakar.
People in Dakar are very friendly and welcoming. They speak French, which is the official language,
and also Wolof, the most common local language. Family is very important in Senegal. People often
live together in big family homes. When you meet someone, you smile and greet them kindly.
Hospitality is a big part of the Senegalese culture.
Part six, music and dance. Music is the heart of Dakar. You can hear music everywhere in taxis,
cafes, markets, and on the beach. Traditional drums, singing, and dancing fill the air.
A popular music style in Dakar is mbalax, created by the famous singer,
Yuson Andor. People love to dance to the rhythm of the drums. At night, many places in Dakar come
alive with music and joy. Part seven, food in Dakar. Food in Dakar is delicious and full of flavor.
The national dish is tia budyan, rice with fish, vegetables, and tomato sauce. It smells wonderful
and tastes amazing. People also enjoy yasas, a dish made with chicken, onions, and lemon.
For dessert, you can try sweet fried dough or tropical fruits like mango and papaya.
And of course, people love to drink a taya, a strong and sweet green tea shared with friends.
Part eight, markets and handicrafts. The markets in Dakar are full of life and color.
You can buy handmade jewelry, wood carvings, and bright fabrics. Local artists paint
scenes of daily life and nature. One of the most famous markets is Marché Sandaga,
full of music and friendly sellers. It's a perfect place to feel the true spirit of Dakar.
Part nine, nature and the ocean. Dakar is on a peninsula surrounded by the ocean. The beaches
are beautiful and full of energy. You can see people swimming, surfing, or playing football
by the sea. There are also quiet beaches where you can relax and listen to the waves. From Dakar,
you can take a boat to Gore Island. Peaceful, calm, and full of history.
Part 10, monuments and landmarks. One of the most famous landmarks in Dakar is the African Renaissance
Monument. It is a giant bronze statue taller than the Statue of Liberty. It shows a man, woman,
and child looking toward the future. It represents the strength and hope of the African
people. You can also visit the mosque of the Divinity, a beautiful white mosque by the sea.
Part 11, life in Dakar. Life in Dakar is lively and social. People work, study, and spend time
together. On weekends, families go to the beach or enjoy music festivals. You can always hear
laughter, singing, and the sound of drums. Even with traffic and noise, people live with joy
and peace in their hearts. Part 12, goodbye from Dakar. Thank you for joining me on this trip
to Dakar, Senegal. It is a city full of rhythm, history, and sunshine. From its warm people to
its beautiful ocean views, Dakar has a special soul. If you ever visit West Africa,
don't miss this city. Goodbye. Or as people in Wolof say,
